Description:
Responsive image markup for Umbraco, driven entirely by configuration. Define breakpoint rule sets once in appsettings.json, then render them anywhere with a tag helper or from Razor: picture elements with per-breakpoint art direction, img tags with srcset and sizes, and responsive CSS background images with focal-point-aware background-position.

Every crop is anchored on the focal point the editor set in the back office. That is the part a CDN cannot do for you: an edge resizer has to guess where the subject of an image is, while Umbraco already knows, because someone chose it. Faces stay in frame at every breakpoint.

Lazy loading is native browser lazy loading plus inline LQIP (Low-Quality Image Placeholder) blur-ups generated at render time, so there is no runtime JavaScript dependency at all: no lazysizes, no bundler, nothing extra to ship. Above-the-fold images can instead be marked to load eagerly at high fetch priority, and they register preload hints that a single tag helper emits in your layout head, which is what actually moves your Largest Contentful Paint.

A strict Content Security Policy is supported first class: pass a nonce and the placeholder styles and scripts are emitted as nonce-tagged blocks instead of inline attributes. Rendered markup and resolved rule sets are cached, and the cache is invalidated automatically when content or media changes, including through the cache refreshers that reach every node in a load-balanced setup.

Optionally, hand the resizing off to the edge: point a rule set at Cloudflare Image Transformations and the package composes Cloudflare image URLs, focal point and all, instead of asking your origin to crop. Optional CDN cache purging drops replaced images from the edge when an editor saves new media. Both are off by default.

The package ships a JSON schema for full appsettings IntelliSense and auto-registers through an Umbraco composer, so installing it and adding one addTagHelper line is the whole setup.
Title: Responsive Images
